instruction: Pick up the upright red cola can near the physical right R5 arm with the black wrist camera. Use only that right arm, verify retention with a small visible lift, and keep holding for operator handoff. Do not pick up the tennis ball or the brown bottle at the back of the table.
content: This is a new right-arm task with no demonstration. The controlled physical arm is the right R5 in the shared global image, connected to can1. The protocol names its only controllable arm and wrist camera left; those logical names route to this physical right arm and Gemini serial CV2C86100180. The physical left R5 with the white camera is an obstacle and is not controllable in this session.

The red cola container is upright on the tabletop in front of and toward the centre from the right arm. Identify it from fresh global and right-wrist images. Ball_detection metadata, if present, is only an unrelated colour heuristic. It is not localization of the cola target. Prioritize the global view for approach gap, height, support and whole-arm clearance; use the selected wrist for finger placement when consistent. Table cables, tools, papers, the black support, the tennis ball and the other arm must remain clear.

Use the original GPT-Policy Cartesian target and observation loop with the existing R5 official solver and timed trajectory checks. Derive directions from this arm current state and fresh images; no left-arm image response, base-direction mapping or saved joint pose is transferable. The TCP transform and gripper endpoints in this right-arm profile are nominal estimates transferred from the same R5 model, not independently measured calibration. Raw gripper targets increase toward open and decrease toward closed in the vendor convention; empty-gripper opening feedback must be checked before approach. Raw position and current are not a force or jaw-width calibration.

Keep the gripper open during approach. Close only when both views support the object between opposing inner finger surfaces at a viable insertion depth; do not infer contact from image overlap or a stall. Use smaller closing increments near the can, avoid visibly deforming it, and stop if it tips or clearance is lost. Closure alone is not success. Verify the object leaves its support and remains held before reporting done. Finish in powered hold for operator handoff without automatic opening, homing or moving the other arm.
